data.title: Jaguar Health Faces Nasdaq Delisting Over Listing Concerns
data.description:
Jaguar Animal Health ( (JAGX) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 20, 2026, Nasdaq staff notified Jaguar Health, Inc. that it had determined to delist the company’s common stock under Listing Rule 5101, citing public-interest concerns. The concerns involved a September 17 reverse stock split to avoid noncompliance with the $1 bid-price requirement, followed shortly by a special dividend of Series R convertible preferred stock that staff viewed as having the effect of a forward split and again leaving the bid price below $1.

Nasdaq staff also cited substantial dilution imposed on shareholders since January 2023. Jaguar Health requested a hearing by the November 27 deadline, which under Nasdaq procedures will stay suspension pending the Panel’s decision; the release said the company could not assure continued listing or compliance with other Nasdaq rules.

data.title: VisionWave Holdings Completes $2 Million Registered Direct Offering
data.description:
VisionWave Holdings ( (VWAV) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 25, 2026, VisionWave entered an agreement with investors for a registered direct offering of units and pre-funded units accompanied by common warrants. The initial closing occurred on November 27, generating approximately $2 million in gross proceeds before placement-agent fees and other offering expenses; the common warrants initially carried a $0.57 exercise price and were immediately exercisable for five years.

If reset to the $0.0475 floor, the common warrants would cover up to 126,315,756 shares on cash exercise or 189,473,634 shares on alternative cashless exercise. The use of offering proceeds, equity issuance, reverse-split announcements and certain insider dispositions were subject to restrictions and exceptions, while VisionWave’s November 24 waiver with YA II included a conversion standstill, a maturity extension to June 30, 2027, and a November 25 payment of $5.25 million applied primarily to principal.

data.title: Carnival Amends CEO’s Performance-Based Restricted Stock Award
data.description:
Carnival ( (CCL) ) has shared an announcement.

On November 24, 2026, Carnival Corporation Ltd.’s Compensation Committee approved an amendment to CEO Josh Weinstein’s special performance-based restricted stock unit grant made in August 2022. The amendment aligned the award’s performance conditions with those of the fiscal 2024 executive grant, set the performance period to end on November 30, 2026, rather than November 30, 2027, and set vesting for December 2026.

The amended award uses 2026 Adjusted ROIC, adjusted EBITDA per available lower berth day and greenhouse gas intensity reduction goals established in fiscal 2024. It reduced the maximum payout from 200% to 180%, or 900,000 shares, set vesting for December 21, 2026, subject to continued employment, required share retention until December 21, 2028, and added a clawback if Weinstein voluntarily resigns before February 15, 2028.

data.title: Grown Rogue Announces New York Cannabis Acquisition Agreement
data.description:
Grown Rogue International ( (TSE:GRIN) ) has shared an update.

On November 23, 2026, Grown Rogue New York, LLC, a 51%-owned subsidiary, signed membership-interest and asset purchase agreements with PharmaCann and related parties to acquire 100% of PharmaCann of New York’s membership interests and other business assets, including its New York cannabis licenses, Hamptonburgh cultivation and processing facility, and four dispensaries. Completion remained subject to Office of Cannabis Management approval and other closing conditions.

Closing required OCM approval of GRNY as a true party in interest and transfer of license control, simultaneous completion of both agreements, treatment of unpaid taxes, lien releases and no material adverse effect on PCNY. The purchase price was $1.8 million in cash, reduced from $3.1 million for PharmaCann’s 50% share of an approximately $2.4 million New York adult-use cannabis tax assessment and $0.1 million of equipment lease reimbursements. Under an August 20, 2026 agreement, GRNY agreed to provide operational, general and administrative consulting and a secured working-capital line of credit of up to $9.0 million; by November 23, it had begun supporting the operating transition, including cultivation restart at Hamptonburgh.

data.title: PetMed Express Implements Tax Benefit Preservation Rights Plan
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Petmed Express ( (PETS) ).

On November 24, 2026, PetMed Express’ board authorized a dividend of rights tied to its common stock and adopted Articles of Amendment establishing the rights of a new Series B participating preferred stock. On November 25, the company adopted a Tax Benefit Preservation Plan, under which one right was designated for each common share held on the December 7 record date, with a $7 exercise price.

On November 27, the company said the plan was effective immediately and ended its prior limited-duration rights plan by moving expiration from December 2 to 12:01 a.m. that day; all prior rights then expired without payment. The new plan was intended to reduce the risk that an ownership change under Section 382 would limit PetMeds’ estimated $43.4 million in federal net operating loss carryforwards, with unauthorized ownership of 4.9% or more potentially triggering dilution; rights expire no later than November 25, 2029, unless ended earlier under the plan.
